interface.signature: logistic_map(width: int, height: int, x_coords: List[int], y_coords: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]

preconditions.description: The width of the map is between 1 and 100.
The height of the map is between 1 and 100.
The x coordinates are within the map width.
The y coordinates are within the map height.
The number of supply points is equal to the number of x and y coordinates.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(row, list) and len(row) == width for row in result)
postconditions.description: The result is a two-dimensional list with the same width as the map.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(cell, int) or cell is None for row in result for cell in row)
postconditions.description: Each cell in the result contains either an integer distance or None.

postconditions.expression: result == None if not x_coords and not y_coords else all(result[y][x] == min(abs(x - x_coord) + abs(y - y_coord) for x_coord, y_coord in zip(x_coords, y_coords)) for y in range(height) for x in range(width))
postconditions.description: The value of each cell is the Manhattan distance to the nearest supply point, or None if there are no supply points.
